data.cleaned_text: The JSDF has revealed details about their participation in Talisman Sabre 2025: (translation below). [Translation] Participation in the U.S.- and Australia-led Multinational Joint Exercise Talisman Sabre 25 The Japan Self-Defense Forces (JSDF) will participate in the U.S.- and Australia-led multinational joint exercise Talisman Sabre 25 as outlined below. This exercise, co-hosted by the United States and Australia, has been held biennially since 2005 and will mark its 11th iteration. For the JSDF, this will be the sixth participation since its first involvement in 2015. Through this exercise, the JSDF aims to maintain and enhance its joint operational capabilities while strengthening cooperation with participating nations to contribute to the creation of a desirable security environment for Japan. Details Objective: To participate in the U.S.- and Australia-led multinational joint exercise Talisman Sabre 25, enhance and maintain the JSDF’s joint operational capabilities, strengthen cooperation and trust with the armed forces of the U.S., Australia, and other Indo-Pacific countries, and contribute to regional peace and stability. Period (planned): From Sunday, July 13 to Monday, August 4, 2025 LocationAustralia (Queensland and New South Wales) and surrounding maritime and airspace areas Participating countries (excluding Japan)United States, Australia, Canada, Fiji, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Thailand, Tonga, and the United Kingdom Participating JSDF units: Approximately 1,500 personnel from - the Joint Staff Office; - Joint Operations Command; - Ground Staff Office; - Ground Component Command; - JGSDF Eastern Army; - JGSDF Central Army; - JGSDF Western Army - JGSDF Fuji School; - JGSDF Air Defense Artillery School; - Maritime Staff Office; - JMSDF Fleet Escort Force; - Air Staff Office; - JASDF Air Defense Command; - JASDF Space Operations Group; - Iruma JSDF Hospital; - JASDF Logistics Headquarters; - Izumo-class destroyer JS Ise; - JS Suzunami; - Tank landing ship JS Ōsumi Exercise components: (1) Maritime operations training (2) Amphibious operations training (3) Land combat training (4) Live-fire training (5) Space operations training (6) Joint medical support training

[6:09PM] #OpebiAllen #TrafficUpdate 

Obafemi Awolowo Way is good from Radio Junction inward Allen Intersection and Olowu, but slightly congested toward Ikeja Under Bridge.
Ikeja Under Bridge to Allen Intersection is good traffic flow.
Allen Intersection to Radio Junction is busy traffic conditions.
Busy traffic on Aromire Road, both inward and outward, at Allen Intersection.
Good traffic movement on Kudirat Abiola Way, from Ojota inward to Walfare Junction, Ikosi Junction, and down to Radio Junction, with a similarly smooth return journey.
Opebi Link Bridge inward and outward traffic is flowing well at Walfare Junction.
Opebi Road from Shareton Link Bridge inward to Salvation is good traffic flow.
Congested traffic on Opebi Road from Salvation to Opebi Roundabout and Toyin.
Smooth traffic flow from Allen Intersection back to Toyin, Opebi Roundabout, and down to Shareton Link Bridge.

#FollowLASTMA

data.raw_text:
[6:16PM] #Idumota #TrafficUpdate 

Significant traffic congestion at Oyebanji Roundabout route connecting Adeniji Adele Road via Oba's Palace and Police Post, resulting from ongoing construction activities.
Heavy traffic volume at Tinubu Square, extending to Nnamdi Azikiwe Street en route Tom Jones Intersection, due to the influx of commuters during the evening rush hour.
Slow traffic movement beneath Idumota Bridge, specifically on the inward journey to Eyin Eyo and connecting to Balogun and Martins Streets, attributed to market activities and frequent bus stops in the area.
Fluid traffic flow observed on Illubinrin ascending Carter Bridge, with a smooth inward journey to Ijora Olopa, as well as on the Oyingbo route.

#FollowLASTMA
